issues.failure_explanation: At q=0 the strict inequality requires a nonnegative norm to be negative, so M(0) is empty. Consequently the advertised exact-manifold specialization is not obtained, and no probability distribution can be supported on that domain.

failure_location.quote: When $q=0$, one recovers the exact manifold regression model where functions are supported exactly on a low-dimensional manifold.

issues.overall_effect: The claimed q=0 regression regime is absent; the approximation assertion there is vacuous and the sampling premise is impossible.
issues.title: The defined zero-radius tube is empty, not the manifold

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^n$ are $n$ i.i.d samples from a distribution $P$ supported on $\mathcal{M}(q)$, and their corresponding function values are $\{f(x_i)\}_{i=1}^n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The observations have exact responses, and the theorem supplies only an upper bound, not a minimax lower bound. Even after correcting M(0), the asserted rate is not a noiseless minimax characterization: for d=alpha=1 on a circle, nearest-neighbour interpolation has squared risk O(n^{-1}) uniformly over sampling laws, and O(n^{-2}) for the uniform law, rather than n^{-2/3}.

failure_location.quote: In the exact manifold case when $q=0$, Theorem \ref{thmGeneralization} gives rise to the min-max regression error \citep{gyorfi2006distribution}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the minimax identification. A replacement optimality claim requires analysis of the noiseless minimax problem, or a different observation-noise model and a matching lower bound.
issues.overall_effect: The minimax-optimality interpretation is unsupported and incorrect for the stated observation model; this does not by itself refute the upper bound.
issues.title: A noiseless regression upper bound is advertised as minimax
issues.why_classification: The source-supported resolution abandons the optimality guarantee; retaining it requires a different statistical analysis and potentially a different rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By choosing $\delta$ such that $\left(1+L\left (\frac{72}{(1-q)^{2}}\right)^\alpha\right)\delta^\alpha=\epsilon$, we get $\delta=O(\epsilon^{1/\alpha})$

issues.failure_explanation: Writing C_alpha=1+L(72/(1-q)^2)^alpha, the chosen scale is delta=(epsilon/C_alpha)^{1/alpha}. Thus delta^{-d}=C_alpha^{d/alpha} epsilon^{-d/alpha}, and the weight bound similarly acquires C_alpha^{(2d+8)/alpha}. These constants can diverge exponentially as alpha tends to zero, although alpha is excluded from the permitted hidden dependencies.

issues.why_classification: This is a limited weakening of quantitative uniformity; the epsilon and sample-size exponents can remain unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The asserted lower bound fails under the stated scale condition. Take a circle of radius r=1/4 centred in the unit square, q=.99, delta=.4r, and eight equally spaced net points. This is a maximal delta-separated net. At the angular midpoint between two centres, choose x with radial distance 1.98r from the circle centre; x lies in M(q). Its squared distance to the nearest net point is r^2[.98^2+2(1.98)(1-cos(pi/8))], greater than (pr)^2 with p=.995. Every bump is therefore zero, so eta is undefined.

issues.failure_explanation: The class does not fix E, which can have D d_embed ell free coefficients, yet the exponent of 1/delta is independent of ell. A concrete contradiction uses D=1 and N=ell-1 embedding slopes u_j: a constant number of blocks and heads implements clip_[0,1](sum_j ReLU(u_j x-1)). For distinct u_j near 1, clipping is inactive on [0,1] and this is a locally N-dimensional family of independently movable knots. Its covering exponent is at least N, exceeding the lemma's fixed exponent when ell is sufficiently large.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the embedding parameters, and any trainable positional encoding, in the entropy exponent; alternatively explicitly fix these maps. For the main chosen architecture, the additional D ell count has the same stated polynomial order.
issues.overall_effect: The entropy bound is false for the transformer class as defined, so its use for statistical complexity requires a corrected parameter count or a restricted class.

issues.why_classification: A contained correction to the class definition and entropy calculation can preserve the main sample-size rate, but the general covering lemma cannot stand as written.

issues.failure_explanation: Bounded weights and final outputs do not bound intermediate activations. With one token, constant width and four heads, a block can cube two data coordinates while cancelling their linear residuals. After s such blocks and a final clipping FFN, the class contains T_t(x)=clip_[0,1]((2+x-t)^{3^s}-2^{3^s}) with uniformly bounded parameters. Translating t over a fixed interval gives a constant-separation packing of size exp(c 3^s), because transition widths are of order 1/(3^s 2^{3^s}). For fixed remaining architecture parameters, the claimed bound gives log covering number only O(L_T^3), contradicting this packing when L_T=s+O(1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive a covering estimate from the actual cubic activation and parameter-sensitivity recurrences, allowing an exponential-in-depth factor such as 3^{L_T} up to layer factors. Reapply it to the main logarithmic-logarithmic depth choice.
issues.overall_effect: The stated depth dependence of the entropy estimate is false even with a fixed embedding and globally bounded decoded output.
issues.title: The covering bound underestimates depth growth of uncapped cubic attention
issues.why_classification: A new contained entropy argument is necessary. At the main depth O(d+log log n), exponential-in-depth growth is still polynomial in log n, so the stated sample-size exponent can survive.
